name: Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Progressive Myoclonic Epilepsy

criteria.description: Presence of progressive myoclonic seizures characterized by sudden, brief, involuntary muscle jerks
Occurrence of generalized tonic-clonic seizures often refractory to treatment
Progressive neurological deterioration including cognitive decline and ataxia
EEG showing generalized spike-wave and polyspike-wave discharges with background slowing
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with PME (e.g., EPM2A, EPM2B, CSTB)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive myoclonic seizures, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and progressive neurological decline
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by EEG findings and genetic testing but primarily clinical

pathognomonic.notes: Sudden, brief, involuntary muscle jerks worsening over time
Progressive impairment in memory, attention, and executive function
Progressive gait and limb coordination difficulties

common.notes: Often refractory to standard antiepileptic drugs
Abnormal EEG response to photic stimulation
searchTerms: EEG showing reaction to flashing lights

common.notes: Muscle weakness secondary to neurological involvement
Slurred or slow speech due to motor impairment

occasional.notes: Sensory deficits or paresthesias in distal limbs
Mood disturbances associated with chronic illness
Myoclonic jerks precipitated by voluntary movement

rare.notes: Rare episodes of hallucinations or delusions
Enlarged liver in some genetic subtypes

laboratory: Elevated lactate in cerebrospinal fluid in some subtypes
imaging: MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy in advanced stages
EEG with generalized spike-wave and polyspike-wave discharges
genetic: Pathogenic variants in EPM2A, EPM2B (NHLRC1), CSTB genes
Other gene mutations depending on PME subtype
other: Muscle biopsy may show nonspecific neurogenic changes
Skin biopsy for Lafora bodies in Lafora disease subtype

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including muscle and cardiac symptoms

redFlags: Rapidly progressive myoclonic seizures refractory to treatment
Early onset cognitive decline with ataxia
Generalized spike-wave discharges with background slowing on EEG
references: Minassian BA. Progressive myoclonus epilepsies: an update. Epilepsia. 2001;42 Suppl 3:42-51.
Kälviäinen R, et al. Progressive myoclonic epilepsies: disease mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives. Lancet Neurol. 2017;16(1):88-100.
